title: Complications in Assisted Reproduction: Clinical and Perinatal Outcomes
subject: ss-reproductive-medicine
refs: Gardner Textbook of Assisted Reproductive Technologies 5e Ch 24
ASRM Practice Committee Opinion on Elective Single Embryo Transfer

steps.say: A dramatic escalation in heterotopic pregnancy represents a hallmark complication of assisted conception. While naturally occurring in only 1 in 30,000 spontaneous pregnancies, the incidence surges to 1 in 100 to 1 in 500 clinical conceptions following multi-embryo in vitro fertilization transfer.
steps.tx: The occurrence of a **heterotopic pregnancy** (simultaneous coexistent intrauterine and ectopic gestational sacs) demonstrates a steep rise following assisted conception. From a rare baseline **spontaneous conception rate** of 1 in 30000 pregnancies, the documented **ART incidence** climbs dramatically to 1 in 100 to 1 in 500 cycles due to multi-embryo transfer and high-volume transcervical catheters.

steps.say: Despite direct intrauterine embryo placement, ectopic pregnancy complicates 1.5 to 3 percent of all clinical in vitro fertilization pregnancies. Reflux of transferred embryos or underlying tubal cilia dysfunction frequently directs implantation into the ampulla or the dangerous interstitial cornual segment.
steps.tx: Clinical data reveal that **ectopic pregnancy in IVF** occurs with an **incidence rate** of 1.5 to 3 percent of clinical conceptions. Retrograde flushing of transfer media and pre-existing tubal inflammation predispose blastocysts to migrate laterally, resulting in tubal ampullary or hazardous **interstitial ectopic** implantations prone to catastrophic late myometrial rupture.

rows: Classic triad: pelvic pain, amenorrhea, vaginal bleeding
Myometrial expansion; massive hemorrhage upon rupture at 8-12 weeks
Implantation on prior uterine hysterotomy scar; risk of accreta
Unusual implantation directly on surface serosa or ovarian stroma

steps.say: Transvaginal oocyte pickup is generally safe but carries well-recognized procedural hazards. Potential complications include pelvic infection in about 0.5 percent, bowel or ureteral puncture, and severe hemoperitoneum from iliac or ovarian vessel laceration in 0.1 percent.
steps.tx: Transvaginal **oocyte pickup complications** arise from ultrasound-guided needle puncture across the vaginal fornices. While transient bleeding is common, severe intra-abdominal **hemoperitoneum** occurs in 0.1 percent from iliac or ovarian vessel injury, while **pelvic infection** or pelvic abscess complicates approximately 0.5 percent of procedures, requiring prophylactic asepsis.

nodes.label: Transvaginal needle aspiration of mature follicles under ultrasound guidance
Careful Doppler mapping avoids internal iliac and uterine vascular branches
Prompt recognition and surgical intervention if post-procedure hemoperitoneum develops

steps.say: Adopting elective single embryo transfer has revolutionized modern assisted reproductive technology. Routine single blastocyst transfer slashes multiple pregnancy rates from greater than twenty-five percent to less than two percent, completely preserving cumulative live birth outcomes across subsequent frozen cycles.
steps.tx: The widespread adoption of **elective single embryo transfer** (eSET) serves as the primary tool for **multiple pregnancy reduction** in assisted reproduction. Replacing historic multi-cleavage transfers with eSET reduces multiple gestations from >25 percent to <2 percent while fully preserving the **cumulative live birth** rate when surplus embryos are vitrified.

left.title: Elective Single Embryo Transfer (eSET)
points: Single top-quality blastocyst transferred into uterine cavity
Drastic reduction in twin and triplet multiple pregnancies (<2%)
Virtually eliminates maternal pre-eclampsia, preterm birth, and NICU admissions

right.title: Double / Multiple Embryo Transfer
points: Transfer of 2 or more embryos in fresh or frozen cycles
High rate of multiple pregnancy (>25%) with elevated obstetric risks
Marginal gain in single-cycle pregnancy but substantial neonatal morbidity

steps.say: Frozen embryo transfer is associated with distinctive perinatal outcomes compared to fresh transfers. While frozen cycles reduce low birth weight and preterm delivery, they demonstrate an increased incidence of large-for-gestational-age infants and maternal hypertensive disorders of pregnancy.
steps.tx: Evaluating **FET perinatal outcomes** demonstrates key differences compared with fresh IVF. Children conceived from frozen embryo transfers experience reduced rates of small-for-gestational-age and low birth weight, but show an elevated frequency of **large for gestational age** (macrosomia) and an increased maternal **pre-eclampsia risk**, particularly in artificial programmed cycles lacking a functional corpus luteum.

rows: Higher pre-eclampsia risk in programmed cycles

steps.say: Monozygotic twinning occurs significantly more often following blastocyst transfer than after cleavage-stage transfer. Splitting of the inner cell mass during prolonged in vitro culture or following zona pellucida micromanipulation elevates the monozygotic twin rate to 1.5 to 2.5 percent.
steps.tx: Spontaneous **monozygotic twinning** occurs in 1.5 to 2.5 percent of conceptions following **blastocyst transfer**, representing a 2 to 3-fold elevation over cleavage-stage transfers. Mechanical zona pellucida disruption during ICSI or laser hatching and **inner cell mass splitting** during prolonged extended in vitro culture drive this distinct twin phenomenon.

nodes.label: Extended day 5 culture or laser assisted hatching alters zona architecture
Herniating blastocyst experiences mechanical pinching or inner cell mass splitting
Results in monozygotic monochorionic twinning in 1.5 to 2.5 percent of transfers

steps.say: Extensive international epidemiological registries provide robust reassurance regarding the long-term safety of ovarian stimulation. Multi-decade follow-up studies confirm that fertility medications and in vitro fertilization do not increase the invasive risks of ovarian, breast, or endometrial cancers.
steps.tx: Reassuring evidence from comprehensive **epidemiological follow-up** studies confirms long-term **ovulation induction safety**. Rigorous multi-center cohort analyses confirm that repeated gonadotropin stimulation and IVF cycles do not elevate lifetime invasive **cancer risks** for ovarian, breast, or endometrial carcinomas compared with nulliparous, age-matched infertile controls.

steps.say: Children conceived through assisted reproduction show a small relative increase in rare epigenetic disorders. Conditions such as Beckwith-Wiedemann and Angelman syndromes are linked to subtle alterations in DNA methylation established during gamete manipulation or in vitro embryo culture.
steps.tx: Long-term pediatric surveillance identifies a slight relative increase in rare **genomic imprinting disorders** among ART offspring. Epigenetic abnormalities, including **Beckwith-Wiedemann** syndrome, Angelman syndrome, and Silver-Russell syndrome, alter fundamental **epigenetics** and DNA methylation, reflecting subtle vulnerabilities during gamete micromanipulation or in vitro embryonic culture stages.

left.title: Beckwith-Wiedemann Syndrome
points: Overgrowth syndrome with macroglossia, omphalocele, and hemihypertrophy
Loss of maternal methylation at KCNQ1OT1 (KvDMR1) locus on 11p15
Elevated risk of pediatric embryonal tumors (Wilms tumor, hepatoblastoma)

right.title: Angelman Syndrome
points: Severe neurodevelopmental disorder with ataxia, microcephaly, and paroxysms
Loss of maternal expression of UBE3A gene on chromosome 15q11-q13
Higher proportion of imprinting defects observed in ART-conceived cases
